The famous quotation by Edmund Wilson says, "No two persons ever read the same book." I think the author means that every person has their own life experience. Because of this, people notice different things in the same story and feel different emotions.

I completely agree with this statement. When we read, we connect the story with our own life. A teenager and an adult will look at the same characters in completely different ways.

A good example is the novel "Fathers and Sons" by Ivan Turgenev. The main character, Bazarov, rejects art, love, and family traditions. For a young reader, Bazarov often looks like a strong hero and a cool rebel who is not afraid to say what he thinks. But for an older reader, like a parent, Bazarov might seem rude and too confident. They can see that his ideas are actually wrong and bring him a lot of pain in the end. So, two people read the same book, but one likes the hero, and the other does not understand him.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that Wilson is right. Our interpretation of a book depends on our age and experience, which makes reading a very personal thing for everyon
